First let me state I have been making my own home made mixes for years, about 2 years ago I finally bought a stand juicer. I use it 2 to 3 times per month. Even home bartending gets crazy if you have to juice a lot of citrus by hand. (Hamilton Beach 932 Commercial Citrus Juicer)

On to my sour mix.

  • I start with 2 glass bottles about 70% full of water. (About 34 oz bottle size)
  • 1 1/2 cups of sugar.
  • Bring sugar and water to boil on stove.
  • After boil remove from heat.
  • Add 1 bunch fresh Rosemary, 1 bunch Fresh Thyme.
  • At this point I use a big tray and transfer it to the freezer to cook quickly.
  • Juice about 6 to 8 Lemons, and about 8 to 10 limes.
  • Once liquid is cooled mix Juice in to taste. Looking for a balance of sweet and sour.
  • Note, do not dip tasting spoon into mix. I use small ladle and but liquid into small dish to taste. That way I do not cross contaminate the product.
  • Strain, and bottle up. Any extra juice can be used for cocktails that night. Overflow liquid might need and extra container.

I use this for a ton of drinks, but you can make a quick awesome 'Rita with this. 5 parts Tequila, 3 parts cointreau, 3 to 4 parts sour mix. Add ice and enjoy.
There is nothing about fresh juice used in recipes! Especially the combination with fresh Rosemary and Thyme sounds awesome
Thank you! I use this for many, many drinks. Whisky Sour, margaritas, and most anything I can come up with. Great for gin and tonic, although fresh Thyme sprig in a G&T is a bit better.
To clarify; you want to only cool the sugar water and not freeze it. And what does the tray do? Help cool?
The increased surface area of the tray will help speed the cooling process.

Exactly, I have not timed it, but it cools much faster then leaving it in the pot. This is also a kitchen type of thing. I don't want say trick, because using cooling trays is required in professional kitchens to avoid bacteria growth in food. 40 to 140 F is the bad range (approx) and the health department wants you to move food through that range as quickly as you can when cooking.
